name: xhostd
description: Deploy websites, APIs, and services to xhostd from your coding agent. Create projects, push code, deploy previews or production, inspect status, and manage environments, services, variables, storage, and domains.

interface.longDescription: Use xhostd from ChatGPT or Codex to create projects, write and push code, deploy previews or production to HTTPS URLs, run a web process and a worker as services of one project, read deploy and runtime logs, and manage environments, variables, secrets, database snapshots, and custom domains through an OAuth-authenticated MCP server. It serves developers, and anyone who wants a site or an app online without running a server. Limitations: in a client with no shell, code reaches a project as file commits, with no git push; a secret's value is entered in the xhostd console or uploaded from a shell, never in the chat; and plan changes, payments, member invitations, and git host connections happen in the xhostd console, not through the plugin.
defaultPrompt: Create a one-page site on xhostd and put it online
Show my xhostd projects and their live URLs
Why did my latest xhostd deploy fail?

positive.description: The user asks for the live URL of an existing project.
positive.prompt: List my xhostd projects and give me the live URL of review-site.
positive.expected_behavior: Names review-site and gives its HTTPS hostname, read from the environment object.

positive.description: The user creates a new static site and puts it online.
positive.prompt: Using xhostd, create a static project called hello-review with a one-page site that says Hello, and put it online.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the project, or reuses hello-review when it already exists from an earlier run. Commits index.html with commit_files, deploys the returned sha, and polls get_logs until the status is success. Returns the URL.

positive.description: The user edits a page of an existing project and redeploys it.
positive.prompt: On xhostd, add a line with today's date under the heading of review-site's home page, and redeploy it.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the page, adds the date line under the heading with commit_files edits, deploys the commit, and confirms that the deploy succeeded.

positive.description: The user adds a secret to a project without sharing its value in the chat.
positive.prompt: On xhostd, add a secret named API_KEY to review-site.
positive.expected_behavior: Never asks for the value in the chat. Gives the console link with the key filled in, or, in a client with a shell, the upload command that reads the value from a file.

positive.description: The user connects a custom domain to a project.
positive.prompt: On xhostd, connect the domain review-site.lifshitz.io to review-site.
positive.expected_behavior: Attaches the domain to review-site's prod environment; the domain is already attached, so the call changes nothing. Relays the domain's status and DNS records word for word.

negative.description: The request is unrelated to hosting, so the plugin does not trigger.
negative.prompt: Book me a flight to Lisbon next Tuesday.

negative.description: The request is a coding question that needs no hosting, so the plugin does not act.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a string.
negative.expected_behavior: No xhostd tool is called. The assistant answers in the chat.

negative.description: The user asks for a plan change and a payment, which the plugin does not make.
negative.prompt: Upgrade my xhostd plan and pay with my card.
negative.expected_behavior: No xhostd tool is called. The assistant says it cannot change plans or take payments, asks for no card details, and shows no plans or purchase link.

publication.release_notes: xhostd 0.80.1 for ChatGPT and Codex: create projects, commit code, deploy to HTTPS URLs, read logs, and manage variables, secrets, and custom domains. What changed in 0.80.1: the skill's example install.sh drops a comment, and no tool changes. What changed in 0.80.0: an app is now a project, a channel is an environment, and an env var is a variable, and each tool takes the new name, such as list_projects, create_project, update_environment, and set_variable; a project can run several services, such as a web process and a worker, with create_service, update_service, delete_service, and restart; update_service can rename a service, and each old address keeps working for 30 days; rename_database and rename_bucket set the label that names a database or a bucket in listings; XHOSTD_DOMAINS also lists each environment's full address; the guides describe services and the new addresses of a transferred project; the docs name cname.xhostd.app as the CNAME value of a custom domain; and every earlier tool name and argument name still runs for now and is deprecated. Error details and deploy log lines still use the earlier names app and channel.
